simple.meaning: מְנוּסָה (mᵉnûwçâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “retreat.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Leviticus, Isaiah, beginning at Leviticus 26:36. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְנוּסָה (H4499) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מְנוּסָה (mᵉnûwçâh) / H4499 is traced through Leviticus 26:36, Isaiah 52:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “ ‘As for those of you who are left, I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a driven leaf will put them to flight; and they shall flee, as one flees from the sword. They will fall when no one pursues.
